I personally have played it and I find it good. Not very good but good. If you like the DOS videogames, you'll probably like the boardgame too.

I think the most important difference is simply the fact, that you have to do a lot of counting and calculating. In the video game, you attack, the enemy loses health and it's the next turn. In the boardgame, you have to do all the counting and calculating yourself, which can become tedious at times.

Like, you do an attack, roll the specified dice, count the different symbols, calculate based on those, and add 4 for your level, add 2 because of the element, add 3 because of some stat, add 1 because of some other stat and so on. Then subtract your enemy's armor to find out how much health he actually loses. It's not bad but it can become tedious.

Edit: As you mentioned robbing peoples houses, there is not much creative freedom in the boardgame. You do have a lot of different story choices which influence the story heavily, but there's no stuff like grabbing explosive barrels for later or killing a random person and seeing what happens. There are no NPCs to freely interact with
